rationale:
Evidence: every raced design so far left the track in all 60 development trials. max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit, rms_error is about 0.03, and steering_oscillation is small (0.06 to 0.15), so the robot drifts steadily to the edge rather than jittering. The best race (iteration 5, score 53.64) was the wide 7-sensor array with kd 0.8 and base_speed 0.9. Its progress rose to about 0.14, so raising kd and lowering speed helped. Iteration 3 showed integral action does not fix the drift.

Changes: (1) Keep the iteration-5 wide 7-sensor array (x = -0.075 to +0.075, y = 0.06, size 0.016) and weights. (2) Raise kd from 0.8 to 1.2 to damp overshoot on the bends, since kd is the variable that moved the score most. (3) Narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. For the same PWM difference this raises yaw rate, so the robot can correct faster at the same kp. (4) Lower mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to reduce yaw inertia. Keep kp 4.5, ki 0, base_speed 0.9 and last_direction line loss so the change is mostly kd plus the chassis response.

Expected result: max_error should stay below or near 0.06 with fewer edge exits, and progress should rise above 0.14 on the oval and s-bend. Finishing in 3 s is still unlikely at this speed. If tracking holds, the next revision should raise base_speed toward 1.5.
